chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever swears and says, "No, by the Lord of the Book," and then breaks his oath, upon him is one expiation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath sworn by the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, clarifies that swearing by 'the Lord of the Book' (Rabb al-Mushaf) constitutes a valid oath requiring expiation upon breaking, a ruling attributed to Imam al-Sadiq quoting Imam Ali. It highlights the jurisprudential principle that invoking the Quran as a witness binds the swearer, distinguishing it from casual speech. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for defining the scope of 'Yamin' (oath) when the Quran is explicitly cited as the object of the oath.
